messages:
Maya (CS): heads-up — Eunoia Health just escalated. After our 3.2.0 rollout their discharge-summary pipeline started returning fabricated medication dosages for ~2% of records. They gave examples and say this started exactly after the weekend deploy. :grimacing:

Sam (ML): thanks. do we have the model id they hit and a sample prompt?

Maya (CS): model in use: `redwood-3b-quant-v2` (hosted). API call they showed: 
```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
{
  "model": "redwood-3b-quant-v2",
  "input": "Patient: 72yo male, hx HTN. Meds prior: lisinopril 10mg daily. Discharge instructions: ... (redacted)\n  Please write a concise medication list with dosages for EHR import."
}
```
They get: `lisinopril 20 mg` (wrong dose) in the output for that record. Internal evals (on our standard clinical set) had no regressions. They attached 8 failing prompts, 3 of which flip numeric doses.

deploy-bot: rollout redwood-3b-quant-v2 @ 1765108200 -> traffic 100% :rocket:

Sam (ML): ok. possible candidates: quantization profile tweak, kernel change (FP16->int8 mix), or batching/caching affecting numeric tokenization. Priya — did we change any number-mangling code in this release?

Priya (Model Owner): we changed the quant profile for the 3b family to improve perf under long seqs (less kludgy rounding for float->int mapping). No explicit tokenization changes. We also updated the fused-kernel in runtime that touches sampling math for low-prob events. Both could subtly affect rare numeric outputs. Our unit evals are noisy but within thresholds — nothing flagged.

Maya (CS): customer notes: "Previously outputs matched our templates nearly 100%. Now we see wrong dosages ~2% of the time for long discharge notes (>800 tokens)." They pushed a full example.

Elena (DevEx): can we repro locally with their exact prompt + system context and seed? ask them for the exact full prompt payload + randomness settings (temperature, top_p) and whether they use streaming or chunking. Also will need the request id from their failed calls.

Maya (CS): asked for full request_id list. gave us one: `req_7b43f9a2`. attached the full prompt (redacted PHI). They use `temperature=0.1`, `max_tokens=256`, no streaming.

Sam (ML): reproducing now. quick sanity: run harness with identical tokenization and the same model artifact. I'll spin `repro-harness --model redwood-3b-quant-v2 --seed 42 --input file.json`.

(infra-bot): note — model artifact `redwood-3b-quant-v2` deployed from build `ci/anchor/2026-03-06-14:22`

Sam (ML): initial run with public prompt: no misdosage observed in 100 seeds.

Priya (Model Owner): this smells like a coverage gap. Our clinical eval set contains templated med lists but not many long, freeform discharge notes with nested parentheticals. If customer prompt structure includes numeric context earlier in the doc, caching or prefix reuse could bias predictions.

Jorge (PM): from product POV we need three things fast: 1) repro on our side, 2) gated rollback if we can show customer impact, 3) add failing prompts as golden tests. Can we triage severity vs traffic? Eunoia is on Dedicated Lite — losing trust is bad.

Elena (DevEx): suggestion: run an A/B compare between `redwood-3b-quant-v1` (previous) and `-v2` on the customer's exact payloads. If v1 is clean and v2 bad -> safe rollback. I can patch the repro harness to batch-compare.

Sam (ML): ran A/B with their 8 failing prompts across 100 deterministic seeds each: v1 produced correct dosages in 98% of runs, v2 produced correct dosages in 95% — difference small but consistent for two particular prompts (the long ones).

Priya (Model Owner): small difference but customer-visible. Two hypotheses: 1) quantization altered logits for low-prob numeric tokens, 2) runtime fused-kernel changed sampling tail behavior. We need a log-prob diff around the numeric tokens. Sam — can you pull token-level logprobs for the failing outputs?

Sam (ML): pulling now. attaching snippet: 
```
prompt: ... lisinopril 10mg ...
v1 logprobs around token sequence for "10": -1.2, -1.1, -0.8
v2 logprobs: -2.9, -3.0, -2.7
```
This shows v2 assigns much lower prob to the correct numeric tokens and relatively higher to `20` cluster.

Maya (CS): customer will be unhappy. Any immediate mitigation?

Elena (DevEx): mitigation plan options: 
- short-term: traffic-split rollback for Eunoia to `-v1` (Dedicated route override) — quick config change.
- medium: hotfix to quant profile or revert fused-kernel for 3b family and run full perf regression.
- long-term: expand clinical eval set to include long freeform notes + numeric perturbations, add token-level logprob regression tests.

Priya (Model Owner): agree. We should rollback for Eunoia immediately while we root cause. I'll open a PR to revert the kernel change (bench and test run).

Sam (ML): I'll generate a small failing dataset from their examples and push to `eval/clinical/real_customer_fails/` with deterministic seeds and token-level checks. Add a CI job to fail if logprob delta > 1.0 for numeric tokens.

Jorge (PM): assign owners: Maya -> coordinate customer comms and get more examples/request ids; Priya -> revert PR + follow perf; Sam -> create repro dataset + run logprob diffs; Elena -> set up temp route override and add the prompts to eval harness. I'll coordinate with support for an SLA note.

Maya (CS): noted. I'll tell Eunoia: short-term we can pin their traffic to previous model while we investigate, and we'll share a timeline. Will ask for any extra examples and their full request logs. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: override applied — route `customer:eunoia-health` -> model `redwood-3b-quant-v1` at 1765121800

Maya (CS): customer confirmed rollback helped for the one example they tested. They want root cause and ETA before they enable v2 again.

Sam (ML): in-progress: I have the logprob diffs for the 8 prompts. For two prompts the numeric tokens show >1.5 logprob delta. Attaching a small patch to the eval runner to assert token-level parity across variants.

Priya (Model Owner): launching perf regression tests on kernel revert now. If revert doesn't kill perf, we'll keep it. If it does, we'll try a narrower quant profile rollback.

Jorge (PM): good. next steps: update customer by EOD with findings and expected timeline for permanent fix. Also add these prompts to the public 'clinical stress' suite.

Maya (CS): will do. tagging this thread as follow-up. Thanks everyone. :pray:

Elena (DevEx): action items summarized: 
- repro dataset: Sam (ML)
- eval harness golden tests: Sam + Elena
- kernel/quant revert PR: Priya
- customer comms & extra logs: Maya
- route override applied: infra (done)

Maya (CS): last note — let's make sure we capture whether customer used any pre- or post-processing (our token normalization hooks could be different in Dedicated). I'll ask and add to repro.

Sam (ML): good catch; will compare tokenization outputs between our hosted default and customer's dedicated runtime image.

(end)
